title: Lightroom Export Photo Failure Rate
dataSources: Lightroom photo exports (`lightroom:photo`), Flickr photo metadata (`flickr:photo`), ShutterCount body audits (`shuttercount:camera`), and F3 card tests (`f3:card`).
app: Adobe Lightroom exports, Flickr API metadata, ShutterCount camera audits, and F3 SD-card health checks sent to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lightroom:photo
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(export_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by collection_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Lightroom export photo records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each collection name.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize export_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per collection name.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It maps which parts of your Lightroom export photo data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
